matches.quote: The RB-mixed state therefore persists only while non-zero gate voltages are held inside the bistable window, which is weaker than the usual memory meaning of non-volatility.
Fig. 3a overlays blue contours from a different contact configuration on data from the main configuration. Mark them clearly as such or show them on their own map
The caption assigns the −4.1 and −15.5×10¹² cm⁻² thresholds to "forward and backward scans, respectively"... Check that these agree with the legend arrows.
Reproducibility across devices, regions and cooldowns is unclear... The hysteresis "appears only in part of the device" (Extended Data Fig. 4)
a direct structural probe of the transport device, or of an equivalent device, after it has been set into each state... at minimum KPFM before and after switching.
Gate-hysteretic switching between correlated magnetic and non-magnetic states... has been reported... state precisely what is new: switching driven by a stacking change
The theory–experiment comparison in Fig. 3b is presented as "agree well" or "remarkable", but it is qualitative... plot the calculated ΔU along each experimental contour
domain identification rests on KPFM contrast alone, measured on a different sample... determine the domain stacking in device A directly, for example by Raman
The authors should give its conditions (ambient or not, tip calibration) and the uncertainty of the 22 mV work-function difference.
Device B (0.03° twist) appears only for the AHE sign reversal. The text does not say whether device B shows the gate-driven switching... or the on/off AHE.
Without it, the data are equally consistent with purely electronic bistability in a fixed domain landscape, such as hysteresis between competing correlated states
"First-order quantum phase transition" (p. 2) is not an accurate description... "Gate-driven first-order structural transition" would be more accurate.
They should also discuss how a modest rhombohedral fraction can give an AHE larger than that of a pure rhombohedral device
polar domains break inversion and would give a D-odd AHE without any domain-wall physics... test whether it follows D or the layer that holds the carriers.
The temperature, sweep-rate and retention dependence of the switching is missing... show the switching thresholds versus temperature, up to and above the ~8 K Curie temperature

notes: The review did not have access to Extended Data Figs. 1-11 or the SI (noted in P8), so concerns about specific Extended Data panels (C6, C10, C11, C16) could only be raised indirectly from the main text (C6 and C16 judged partly; C10 and C11 not raised). For C2, P5 still deduced from the main text that device B was only invoked for AHE sign reversal and lacked demonstrated on/off AHE switching. For C15, P15 and P17 propose polar ABAC/ABCB stackings (which are 123- vs 234-rhombohedral) and carrier-layer asymmetry as alternatives for the D-odd AHE, judged partly.
